grammar.title: 给 for giving to someone
grammar.explanation: 给 (gěi) means "to give" or introduces the person something is done "for/to". It comes before the recipient: 我给你 means "I give it to you". Like other simple verbs, it can stand alone in a short sentence.

grammar.title: 不大 for "not very"
grammar.explanation: 不大 (bú dà) means "not very" or "not really", softening a negative statement: 不大喜欢 ("doesn't like very much"), 不大想去 ("doesn't really want to go"). It's a gentler alternative to a flat 不喜欢 or 不想去.

grammar.title: 请 for polite requests
grammar.explanation: 请 (qǐng) makes a request polite, like English "please". It comes at the very front of the sentence, before the person being addressed if one is named: 请你来 ("Please come").

grammar.title: 能 for ability or permission
grammar.explanation: 能 (néng) means "can" — able to do something because of ability, permission, or circumstance. It goes directly before the verb. Negate it with 不能 (bù néng), "cannot".

grammar.title: 有 for possession
grammar.explanation: 有 (yǒu) means "to have". Sentence-final 了 after 有 signals a change: the subject did not have it before but has it now.

sentences.en: He doesn't really want to go.
